identity.title: OpenMathInstruct-1: A 1.8 Million Math Instruction Tuning Dataset

problem.claim: Construct a large-scale, commercially permissive math instruction-tuning dataset using open-source generation pipelines.

gap.claim: Existing large-scale math instruction datasets relied on closed-source LLM outputs, while a skill gap had limited open-source LLMs in comparable generation pipelines.

contributions.claim: OpenMathInstruct-1, a dataset of 1.8M math problem-solution pairs synthesized with Mixtral code-interpreter solutions for GSM8K and MATH.
OpenMath-CodeLlama-70B, trained on a subset of the dataset.
A planned release of the code, models, and dataset under a commercially permissive license.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors identify their prompting approach, combined with brute-force scaling and recent open-source LLM progress, as the novelty behind constructing the dataset.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that OpenMath-CodeLlama-70B scores 84.6% on GSM8K and 50.7% on MATH.
The authors report these scores as competitive with the best GPT-distilled models.

narrative_sequence.summary: Synthetic datasets are presented as useful for teaching targeted LLM skills.
Existing large-scale math datasets use closed-source LLM outputs, and open-source models had lagged mathematically.
The authors combine prompting, scaling, and Mixtral-generated code-interpreter solutions to build a 1.8M-pair dataset.
A CodeLlama-70B model trained on a subset is reported to reach 84.6% on GSM8K and 50.7% on MATH, competitive with GPT-distilled models.
The authors state that code, models, and data will be released under a commercially permissive license.

source_observation.claim: The abstract links dataset accessibility to both the generator model's license and the planned licensing of the resulting code, models, and data.

lessons.interpretation: When a dataset is intended for broad use, provenance and downstream licensing are part of the contribution rather than implementation details.
lessons.application: State the source-model license, generation provenance, and intended redistribution terms alongside the dataset construction description.
lessons.exception: This framing is less central when redistribution rights are already standardized or the work does not release generated artifacts.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the prompting method, scaling procedure, subset composition, training setup, baselines, or evaluation protocols.
The meaning of “competitive” is not quantified beyond the two reported benchmark scores.
